'''Chen Greif''' ({{Langx|he|חן גרייף}}) is a professor and former department head of computer science at the [[University of British Columbia]]. In March 2022 he was elected a fellow of the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] for "contributions to scientific computing, especially in numerical linear algebra and its applications."<ref>{{cite press release |title=SIAM Announces Class of 2022 Fellows |url=https://sinews.siam.org/Details-Page/siam-announces-class-of-2022-fellows |publisher=Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics |date=March 31, 2022}}</ref>

== Education ==
Greif attended [[Tel Aviv University]], earning a bachelor's degree 1991 and a master's degree in 1994 in mathematics. He continued his education at the [[University of British Columbia]], where he was awarded a PhD in Applied Mathematics in 1998. He was also a postdoctoral fellow at Stanford University from 1998 to 2000.<ref>{{cite web |title=Chen Greif - Bio |url=https://www.cs.ubc.ca/~greif/Bio.html |publisher=University of British Columbia |access-date=April 2, 2022}}</ref>

== Research ==
His research is primarily concerning scientific computing and more specifically:
* Matrix theory and analysis
* Iterative solvers and preconditioning techniques for sparse linear systems
* Saddle-point linear systems
* Numerical solution of elliptic partial differential equations
* Linear algebra aspects of constrained optimization problems
